html:
The Yemen cholera outbreak began in October 2016 during Yemen's civil war and became one of the largest outbreaks of the disease in modern history, with well over two million suspected cases and several thousand deaths.

Cholera spreads through water and food dirtied by sewage. The war, which pits the Houthi movement against a government backed by a Saudi-led coalition, had wrecked Yemen's water pumps, sewage works and hospitals. Air strikes and a blockade cut fuel and medicine, health workers went unpaid, and millions were already hungry.

Cases peaked in 2017, one of the fastest-spreading outbreaks on record. In 2017 and 2019 Yemen made up most of the world's reported cholera cases, and children were a large share of the sick. Oral rehydration, clean water and vaccine campaigns from 2018 slowed it.

It follows a long history of the disease, which spread out of Bengal in the 19th century in the cholera pandemics. Compare the earlier links between Yemen and the world through coffee.
sum: The Yemen cholera outbreak began in October 2016 during Yemen's civil war and became one of the largest outbreaks of the disease in modern history, with well over two million suspected cases and several thousand deaths.
